key_idea: Count the triangles first. Circles must be half of that, and squares double that.
steps: Count the shapes in each picture.
Picture B has 2 triangles, 1 circle and 4 squares.
1 circle is half of 2 triangles. 4 squares is twice 2 triangles, because 2 + 2 = 4.

choice_feedback.A: A has 2 triangles and 2 circles. There should be only 1 circle.
choice_feedback.C: C has 4 triangles, so it needs 8 squares, but it has only 2.
choice_feedback.D: D has 2 triangles, so it needs 4 squares, but it has only 2.
choice_feedback.E: E has 4 triangles, so it needs 2 circles and 8 squares, but it has 1 circle and 4 squares.
